title: UBAG Job Event
description: Single event in a job lifecycle event stream or historical event log.

sequence.description: Monotonic sequence number within a job.

data.description: Event-specific payload. Token events carry token deltas and are provisional (see attempt_id); terminal events carry status, result, or error summaries, and only a terminal event of the current attempt produces the job result. Stage timings, when present, ride in the optional timings_ms object (not in JobResponse.metadata).

attempt_id.description: Attempt that produced this event (worker daemon protocol v2). It lives inside data because the event envelope is closed. When present, event_id MUST be derived from it so a retried attempt's events never collide with an earlier attempt's: the reference derivation is evt_ + the first 16 hex chars of sha256(job_id:attempt_id:sequence); without attempt_id it stays sha256(job_id:sequence). Events of one job may mix both forms across a deploy. Semantics: token and token_streaming events are PROVISIONAL, a live view of one attempt that a consumer may discard if that attempt is abandoned (no terminal event, daemon died, lease fenced); the job result comes only from a terminal event of the current attempt, never from concatenated token events.

stream_end_reason.description: Why the provider stream stopped, on the terminal event of a streamed job. Anything other than provider_done means the text is not a complete answer: a deadline cut ends the job timed_out (never completed), with the text under data.partial and not in the result (decision D4).

partial.description: On a timed_out terminal event: what was received before the cut. Informational only; it is never the job result.

submitted.description: On a failed_retryable/failed_terminal/timed_out event: true when the prompt had already been submitted to the provider, so the attempt MUST NOT be blindly resubmitted.

reconcile_required.description: On a failed_terminal event after an ambiguous post-submit failure (decision D4): the provider thread must be reconciled by a read-only check before anyone retries. Only valid together with submitted:true.

timings_ms.description: Optional worker-side stage durations in milliseconds, measured with a monotonic clock (not derived from event created_at, which can be replayed after the run). Closed key set; every key is optional so a stage that did not run is simply absent.

worker_start.description: Worker/runner startup before job work begins.

auth_check.description: Read-only signed-in-state check (safe-mode: never logs in).

provider_submit.description: Prompt entry and submit on the provider page.

provider_stream.description: First token to end of provider stream.

extraction.description: Response extraction and normalization after the stream.
